paragraphs.text: Throne of Eldraine introduces preconstructed decks specifically built for the Standard Brawl format (which used to be called simply "Brawl" at the time), offering both new and experienced players ready-to-play options that showcase the set's themes and mechanics. These 60-card decks combine a mix of Standard-legal cards from Guilds of Ravnica through Throne of Eldraine with a number of exclusive cards unique to the Brawl product line, designed to emphasize both thematic flavor and balanced gameplay. Each deck includes a commander, a curated selection of creatures, spells, and artifacts, and a life wheel to assist with tracking life totals in multiplayer games. The decks were created under the direction of Melissa DeTora from Play Design , with input from a team of external designers representing diverse playstyles and backgrounds to ensure each deck offered a unique strategy and experience for players.

These 60-card decks use cards from throughout Standard , from Guilds of Ravnica all the way through Throne of Eldraine . There are 20 unique cards in these decks that aren't found in Draft Boosters (but they can still be found in Collector Boosters .) Each deck has seven of them — four cards unique to that deck, one card shared with one other Brawl Deck, and two cards shared with each other Brawl Deck. These cards are all legal in Standard, Brawl, and all other formats that allow the latest sets (or at least ones where cards in new sets are legal). A life wheel is included in the packaging. However, this product doesn't come with any printed tokens .

Melissa DeTora from Play Design was in charge of design for the decks. She selected the colors based on needs for Brawl commanders and designed several of the cards. But then she led a team of four designers from around the country, all external to Wizards of the Coast and under contract, to actually design the decks and provide feedback. This crew was a mix of different styles and backgrounds, each trying to grab different aspects of the community. Each designer led the design of a different deck. The four designers were Emma Handy from StarCityGames , Henry Davis (a local player who had done a lot with community building in the Seattle area), Jeremy Geist (runner up of the Great Designer Search 3 ), and Stephanie Schelble (a casual player from New York).
